items.title: 6.1.2 General Form of an Equation of a Circle (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 165-166: Theorem 2 (general form x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0) with proof by completing the square; Note (i) point circle, (ii) imaginary circle

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein circle ki standard form dekhi jis mein centre aur radius saaf nazar aate hain. Lekin exam mein aksar circle khuli hui shakal mein diya jata hai, jaise \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x - 2y - 20 = 0\). Aaj hum yeh seekhenge ke aisi equation kab circle hoti hai, aur us ka centre aur radius kaise nikalte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Shuru standard form se karte hain. \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}\) ki brackets kholein to:
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 2hx - 2ky + (h^{2} + k^{2} - r^{2}) = 0\]
Is se teen baatein saaf hoti hain jo har circle ki equation mein hoti hain: \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients barabar hain, \(xy\) wala koi term nahin, aur baaqi \(x\), \(y\) aur constant terms hain. In coefficients ko \(2g\), \(2f\) aur \(c\) ka naam de dein to neeche wali general form milti hai. \(2g\) aur \(2f\) mein 2 jaan boojh kar rakha gaya hai, taa ke baad mein aadha karna aasaan rahe.
Theorem 2: Equation \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) ...(1), jahan \(g, f, c \in \mathbb{R}\) (real numbers), ek circle ko represent karti hai.

Proof: Hum is equation ko standard form mein badalna chahte hain, kyun ke standard form se centre aur radius seedhe mil jate hain. Is ke liye 'completing the square' (poora square banana) wala tareeqa lagayenge. Pehle \(x\) wale terms ek saath, \(y\) wale ek saath, aur constant ko doosri taraf le jayein:
\[x^{2} + 2gx + y^{2} + 2fy = -c\]
Ab \(x\) aur \(y\) dono ke liye square poora karne ko dono sides mein \(g^{2} + f^{2}\) jama karte hain:
\[(x^{2} + 2gx + g^{2})\]
\[+ (y^{2} + 2fy + f^{2})\]
\[= g^{2} + f^{2} - c\]
Brackets ab poore squares ban gayi hain, is liye
\[(x + g)^{2} + (y + f)^{2} = \left(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\right)^{2}\]
Isi ko standard form ki tarah minus wali shakal mein bhi likh sakte hain:
\[[x - (-g)]^{2} + [y - (-f)]^{2}\]
\[= \left(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\right)^{2}\]
Yeh circle ki equation ki general form hai, jis ka centre \((-g, -f)\) aur radius \(r = \sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\) hai, basharte (provided) \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c > 0\) ho.
Is liye equation (1) circle ko represent karti hai, shart yeh hai ke \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c > 0\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(g^{2}\) hi kyun jama kiya? \(x^{2} + 2gx\) ko poora square banane ke liye \(x\) ke coefficient ka aadha le kar us ka square jama karte hain. \(2g\) ka aadha \(g\) hai, is liye \(g^{2}\) jama kiya aur \((x + g)^{2}\) ban gaya. \(y\) ke liye bhi yahi: \(f^{2}\) jama karo. Aur yaad rakhiye: tarazu ki tarah, jo cheez left side mein daali woh right side mein bhi daalni parti hai, warna equation ka tawazun (balance) bigar jata hai.
Nateeja: centre \((-g, -f)\) yani \(x\) aur \(y\) ke coefficients ka aadha, sign badal kar; aur radius \(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\).
Second degree ki aam equation \(ax^{2} + by^{2} + 2hxy + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) circle tabhi ho sakti hai jab \(a = b \ne 0\) aur \(h = 0\) ho, yani \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients barabar hon aur \(xy\) wala term na ho. Agar \(a = b\) magar 1 nahin, to pehle poori equation ko \(a\) se divide kar lijiye.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
(i) Agar \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c = 0\) ho to equation (1) ek point circle hai jis ka centre \((-g, -f)\) hai.
(ii) Agar \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c < 0\) ho to equation (1) koi real locus nahin deti (imaginary circle).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Note ko yun samjhiye: \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c\) asal mein radius ka square hai. Radius ka square positive ho to asal circle; zero ho to radius zero, yani sirf ek point; aur negative ho to aisa koi real radius hai hi nahin, kyun ke kisi real number ka square negative nahin hota. Is liye pehle hamesha yeh number check kijiye, phir circle ki baat kijiye.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari misaalein hain, kitab ki nahin.)
1. \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y + 13 = 0\): \(2g = -4\) se \(g = -2\), \(2f = 6\) se \(f = 3\), \(c = 13\). Ab \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c = 4 + 9 - 13 = 0\). Yeh point circle hai, point \((2, -3)\). Waqai yeh \((x - 2)^{2} + (y + 3)^{2} = 0\) hai.
2. \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x + 5 = 0\): \(g = 1\), \(f = 0\), \(c = 5\); \(1 + 0 - 5 = -4 < 0\). Koi real point nahin, kyun ke \((x + 1)^{2} + y^{2} = -4\) namumkin hai.
3. \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x - 8y = 0\): \(g = -3\), \(f = -4\), \(c = 0\); \(9 + 16 - 0 = 25 > 0\). Asal circle: centre \((3, 4)\), radius 5. (Ghor kijiye: \(c = 0\) hai, is liye yeh circle origin se guzarta hai.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya \(x^{2} + 2y^{2} - 4x + 1 = 0\) circle hai? (Nahin: \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 aur \(y^{2}\) ka 2 hai; barabar nahin, is liye yeh circle nahin ho sakta.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. General form: \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\).
2. Centre \((-g, -f)\), radius \(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\).
3. \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c > 0\): asal circle; \(= 0\): point circle; \(< 0\): imaginary circle (koi real locus nahin).
4. Second degree equation circle tabhi hai jab \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients barabar hon aur \(xy\) term na ho.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Centre ko \((g, f)\) ya (\(x\) ka coefficient, \(y\) ka coefficient) likh dena; sahi \((-g, -f)\) hai: coefficients ka aadha, sign badal kar.
2. \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 kiye baghair formula laga dena.
3. Radius \(\sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} + c}\) likh dena: constant \(c\) minus hota hai.
